name: LoMa
plain: LoMa (Nordström, Edstedt et al. 2026): sparse matching of two photos of one scene: DaD keypoints, DeDoDe-G descriptions (VGG19 plus DINOv2) and a light LightGlue-style transformer matcher; matches as keypoint index pairs (the form COLMAP takes). MIT code and weights; DINOv2 Apache-2.0.
summary: LoMa (Nordström, Edstedt et al. 2026): local feature matching with a light transformer. DaD (a VGG11 detector trained by distillation, Edstedt et al. 2025) finds 2048 keypoints per image, a DeDoDe descriptor (VGG for B64/B128, VGG plus DINOv2 for B/L/G/R) describes them, and nine LightGlue-style transformer layers (rotary self-attention, cross-attention) refine the descriptions before a dual-softmax assignment. Returns both keypoint sets, the index pairs of the matches and their scores.
limitations: Sparse output: no dense warp. `result.matches()` gives the matched points for `estimate_pose`; `pairs` are the index pairs pycolmap / COLMAP databases take.
One image pair per call internally (batches run pair by pair); the match counts differ per pair.

The match count depends on the image pair. The fixed 768 x 1024 LoMa-B64 TensorRT export returns variable-length matches. On ten photos paired with shifted copies, at least 96.7% of TensorRT correspondences agreed with portable within 2 pixels in both images.
Two resizes per image as upstream: the detector sees a long side of `long_side` (aspect kept), the descriptor a `size` x `size` square whatever the aspect ratio.
LoMa-R uses rotation augmentation. The other variants are trained for upright images.
task_io: Input: two RGB images of one scene. Output: for every pixel of the first image its position in the second (x, y in pixels) and a certainty that the pixel is visible in both. Sparse matchers (LightGlue) return the keypoints of both images and the index pairs of the matched ones instead. To reconstruct camera poses from an image folder with these matchers, see [structure from motion](../sfm.md).

variants.name: loma-b

training_data.name: MegaDepth (Internet photo collections with SfM / MVS depth)

licence.training_note: Matcher: MegaDepth (paper); DaD: MegaDepth-based distillation (DaD paper); DeDoDe-G descriptor: MegaDepth; B, L, G and R include frozen DINOv2 (LVD-142M). B64 and B128 use VGG descriptors.
notes: weights licence not stated by the original authors; assumed to be the code licence

variants.input_size: any H x W >= 32, padded to a multiple of 32

portable.protocol: first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

original16.protocol: median of 5 after 3 warm-up, uint8 CUDA input, original code at the pinned commit, torch.no_grad; peak = max over the first call and the timed calls

quality.title: MegaDepth-1500, every 5th pair, relative pose AUC@5 / @10 / @20 degrees
quality.protocol: Dense matchers: 5000 matches per pair sampled from the warp by certainty (upstream's balanced KDE sampling); sparse matchers: all their matches of one call (LightGlue, XFeat: LightGlue's MegaDepth-1500 setting; LoFTR, DeDoDe: their card defaults). OpenCV essential-matrix RANSAC (0.5 px threshold, normalised by the mean focal length); AUC of the larger of the rotation and translation-direction errors. The same 300 pairs for all modes, so float32 and bfloat16 compare pair for pair.

parity.text: CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 0.011 vs the original. GPU, portable bfloat16 and kernels float16 (the defaults): mean |diff| <= 0.05 and p99 <= 0.6 (absolute error of the output `keypoints1`).
